searches.note: Twenty seven searches of a share of twenty eight, one left unspent, none of them the author's. Twelve were restricted to a house's or a body's own domain (eur-lex.europa.eu with minagric.gr twice, once with winesofgreece.org; santowines.gr twice; estateargyros.com twice; gaiawines.gr twice; hatzidakiswines.gr three times; sigalas-wine.com once) and are read as primary through their summaries; ten kept the house's own domain, and where the author had leant on them its importer's, out so that the second source would be independent; five went to the open web. The three shared searches are the appellation's rules: the share of Assyrtiko, the amendment of 2022 and the Vinsanto and liqueur wine categories. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The appellation's rules went first to the European text and the ministry's specification, then each house to its own domain for its own dates and making, then to the open web with the house's domain kept out for the second source.

Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail was found in no source of this check it was cut or said with less (the kouloura of the Kavalieros block, the house's gloss on the name Thalassitis, the old texts, fermented in tank for Familia, very old vines for the Argyros Vinsanto, never fortified for Vinsanto in general).

Facts of a house's own history told on its own pages stand, hedged as the house's account; the dead with no dates in two sources (the Argyros founder of 1903, the Hatzidakis founder) stay described, and every living person is described.

Sources whose title or address names a living person, a writer's own site or a score were met among the results but are cited neither in the fragment nor as a source of a change here (a Master of Wine's own site on the Argyros harvest of 2021, an encyclopaedia site carrying a writer's first name, a report under a writer's name on the Argyros site). The fragment's sources were not changed; the sources of this check are listed per change and per record.

tested: Founded 1991, the first wine a dry Santorini at Oia: the library's year, matched by Wein.plus, Skurnik and the open search's other summaries; the winery began in the family's cellar and moved to a new building at Oia in 1998 by one account, which the author left out and this check leaves out. Confirmed.

The founder a mathematician from a Santorini family: every account met calls him a mathematician; the boyhood summers are the house's own telling and stay hedged. One encyclopaedia names two partners beside him in 1991 and a shareholder of 2003; not settled, left open.

Kavalieros at Imerovigli, a single block, vines of sixty years and more on their own roots: the house's product page and its 2022 sheet give Imerovigli and sixty years and more; merchants give fifty and more, sixty, and nearly seventy; one places the high vineyard near Fira, beside Imerovigli. Kept as the house's figure, the spread left open.

Kouloura baskets for this block: the house describes kouloura training in its page on the island, in general; neither its Kavalieros page and sheet nor any merchant met tied it to this block. Cut from sites, table and the card.
Eighteen months on fine lees in steel, stirred often at first and less as time passes, no oak: the house's product page and 2022 sheet and three merchants. Confirmed.
Ageing ten years and more: the house's product page and 2022 sheet give an ageing potential of ten years and more. Confirmed.

Kir-Yianni ran the estate from 2020 and bought the majority in 2025 from a company of a Greek shipowner: the house's own news page of 12 November 2025, The Drinks Business and Just Drinks. Confirmed; the shipowner is living and stays unnamed. One trade report dates a first stake of forty per cent to 2009, in one source only; not added.

The Santorini label's at least 85 per cent Assyrtiko: the approved amendment published in the Official Journal in 2022 raised the minimum from 75 to 85 per cent, and the ministry's specification gives 85. Confirmed; older accounts that give 75 are out of date.

The questions: the wine question's key (no oak, eighteen months on the lees) is one right answer with three oak answers of one kind; the story question's 1991 against 1903, 1947 and 1994, each explained. Sound.
The rules: nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, British, no dash. Sound.

tested: Founded 1903 by the founder at Episkopi Gonia: the estate's About page (the brand established in 1903), the Greek Gastronomy Guide and merchants. Confirmed; the founder has no dates in any source and stays described.

The head of the family who took over in 1974: the Greek Gastronomy Guide and Greeka give 1974 and call him the third generation. Confirmed; he stays described.

The new winery in the 2010s keeping the old cellars and the press of 1903: the estate's winery page gives 2017 and the old cellars of the eighteenth century with the press of 1903; another estate page gives 2015 and a trade report 2016. The story's 2010s stands.
Monsignori from vines of more than two hundred years: the estate's page gives a vineyard of about 220 years; a merchant gives over 200, ungrafted. Confirmed as the estate's dating.
Steel and fine lees, no oak, about eleven months for 2022: two listings give eleven months in steel on fine lees, a third ten months for 2022. Changed to ten or eleven months.

No Monsignori from the 2021 harvest: this check's search of the estate's announcement summarised it for the Vinsanto First and Late Release; a writer's report of October 2021, which the brief does not let a record cite, gives Monsignori and Evdemon held back after drought and heat. Ageing more than ten years: the estate's page says Monsignori can age for over ten years. Confirmed.

The Vinsanto in others: the estate's First and Late Release pages give eight parts in ten Assyrtiko with Athiri and Aidani, sun dried for ten days (fourteen for the Late Release), aged in cement vats and then old wooden barrels; the Late Release replaced the former twelve and twenty year bottlings. Changed.

The questions: the wine question's key (old ungrafted vines and the lees) and its distractors hold; the story question's 1974 against 1947, 1991 and 2002, each explained, the 2002 explanation reworded with Santo's change. Sound.
The rules: nobody living named, nothing volatile (the estate's size and its present head stay out), British, no dash. Sound.

tested: Founded 1994 by two agronomists, Thalassitis its first wine: the house's About page gives the two agronomists and 1994; outside accounts give the first Thalassitis as the 1994 release. Confirmed.

The name and the ancient habit: several accounts give the name as of the sea or coming from the sea; one travel guide, with the two trade pieces the author found, ties it to the ancient mixing of wine with sea water. The house's pages, by the author's own report, give no gloss, so the record no longer says the house says it; old texts describe it in some detail is cut.

The tomato factory at Exo Gonia, built early in the twentieth century, making purée until it closed in the 1970s: the house's Santorini pages give a stone industrial building of the beginning of the 1900s, a tomato purée producer for decades until it closed in the 1970s, between Kamari and Monolithos. Confirmed; one outside account's early nineteenth century is wrong against the house.

Nemea in 1997 at Koutsi: the house's Nemea page gives the winery founded in 1997 in its own vineyard at Koutsi, and its About page has the company starting on Santorini and then at Koutsi. Confirmed, the second winery.
The villages and the vine age: Episkopi, Akrotiri and Pyrgos in two merchants' pages and the visit guide; seventy to eighty years in three. Changed from close to eighty by the house's count.

The making: the importer's 2024 sheet gives the grapes chilled and destemmed, about twelve hours on the skins at around 10 degrees Celsius, selected yeasts at 16 to 17 degrees Celsius in steel and no malolactic fermentation; a merchant's 2020 sheet the same cold soak and selected yeasts; a 2017 sheet 16 to 18 degrees. Changed, the selected yeasts added.
The sea cellar from 2009: the house's history speaks of the 2009 harvest's submerged bottles, of which three were rescued; two secondary accounts give 2009 as the start. Kept, the year left open.
The Wild Ferment's vessels: the importer's sheet and a merchant give steel with French oak, American oak and acacia; another sheet adds ceramic vats. Kept.
The oak fermented Thalassitis renamed Nykteri: the house's Nykteri page gives the rename in 2019. Confirmed and dated.

The questions: the wine question's key (Thalassitis, steel) against the Wild Ferment, the Nykteri and the Nemea red, each explained; the story question's sea cellar against acacia, sun drying and Nemea. Sound.
The rules: the two founders are living and described; nothing volatile; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: Founded 1997 at Pyrgos Kallistis, the cave cellar, the first bottles of the 1997 vintage released in 1998: the house's identity page gives all of it; an outside account gives the vineyard planted in 1996 and the winery in 1997, another the first release in 1999. Kept, the release hedged as the house's.

The founder from Crete, at Boutari from 1991: the house's identity page has him chief oenologist at Boutari's Santorini winery before 1997; an outside account has him arrive in 1991 for an internship there and become head oenologist later. Changed: came to work at Boutari in 1991 and rose to chief oenologist.
The wife who ran Boutari's hospitality, her family's vineyard at Pyrgos abandoned after the earthquake of 1956: the house's identity page, uncultivated until 1996. Confirmed as the house's.
Organic and certified: the house's pages. Kept as written; the claim of the island's first certification stays out.
The vineyard above a larger cave in 2000 and the cellar on the road from Pyrgos to Emporio from 2016: the house's identity page. Confirmed.

The founder's death in 2017: the house and several outside accounts, one giving 11 August 2017 at fifty, another 1967 to 2017. Confirmed; the year of birth stands in one source, so he stays described.

The Nykteri's making: the house's Nykteri page gives Megalochori, overripe grapes in a cold room overnight, destemmed, twelve hours on the skins, its own yeasts at 17 to 18 degrees Celsius, twelve months in French oak barrels of several sizes, and more than ten years of ageing; merchants give the same, one at 18 degrees, and an unfiltered bottling. Confirmed.
Nykteri's rule (at least 13.5 per cent alcohol and three months in oak): the shared search gives both in several accounts beside the Wines of Greece page the author cited. Confirmed.

Others: Familia, by the house, is named in 2018 in the founder's honour and fermented with its own yeasts, tank found nowhere; de Louros, by the house, is fermented with its own yeasts in oak after two days on the skins and kept twenty four months on its lees in French oak. Changed.
The questions: the wine question's key and its three wrong styles hold; the story question now asks the post he rose to. Sound.
The rules: the widow and the children are living and described; the founder is described; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: Founded 1947 as the union, its first form in 1911 as the Santorini Vine and Wine Protection Fund: Skurnik and a travel guide give both years with the same name of 1911; the union's own milestones page opens on the fund. Confirmed.
The new winery at Pyrgos in 1992: two outside accounts. Confirmed.

2002: the union's own timeline, in English and Greek, says European legislation gave Vinsanto the Santorini PDO in 2002; the encyclopaedia says the European Union named Santorini as Vinsanto's place of origin and gave the island the sole use of the name, Italy keeping Vin Santo; a merchant's glossary gives a Greek ministerial decision. Reworded to the union's words, the sole use told as other accounts.

Never fortified: the appellation's specification, as amended in 2022, provides beside the naturally sweet wine a liqueur wine of sun dried grapes made with added alcohol, both at least 51 per cent Assyrtiko; the Wines of Greece page on Vinsanto's making says it is made without strong alcohol. The union's pages call its Vinsanto naturally sweet. Changed to say it of Santo's wine.
The rule of at least two years: the specification's minimum of 24 months of oxidative ageing, on Santorini and Thirasia, by the Wines of Greece summary of the European text. Confirmed.

The making: the union's sheets give harvest between 20 and 30 August, six to eight days in the sun (eight to ten on the twenty year page), forty to sixty days of slow fermentation, and for 2020 three years in 225 litre barrels of the fourth and fifth fill; the wine page gives thirty six months, the 2016 sheet six years. Changed: six to ten days, forty to sixty days, used barrels.
Grapes: eighty five parts Assyrtiko to fifteen Aidani on the union's pages. Confirmed as the great majority.

Ageing and others: the 12 Years Ageing is a selection of the 2008, 2009 and 2010 vintages held at least twelve years in French oak, with dates and coffee in its note; the 20 Years Ageing lists a 2002 vintage bottled in 2023. Changed to say so.

The questions: the wine question's key (sun dried grapes, two years) against frozen grapes, grape spirit and noble rot, each a different way to sweetness; the story question's Vinsanto against Nykteri, Liastos and the Italian Vin Santo. Sound after the rewording.
The rules: the general manager met in the sources is living and not named; no price, no score; British; no dash. Sound.
